title: Class Party Budget

scenario.setup: Your class is planning an end-of-year party and needs snacks for 20 students. Your teacher has given you $40 to spend — and put YOU in charge of shopping!
scenario.conflict: Prices vary between stores, and you need enough food for everyone. Every dollar counts. Spend too much and you're over budget. Spend too little and students go hungry.
scenario.objective: Plan the perfect snack table for 20 students without going over $40

learningObjective: Compare prices, calculate totals using multiplication and addition, and make budgeting decisions with limited funds

questions.text: You need juice boxes for all 20 students — one each. Store A sells a 10-pack for $4.50. Store B sells a 10-pack for $3.80. How much do you save in total by choosing Store B?
questions.hint: You need 2 packs (10 + 10 = 20 students). Find the price difference per pack, then multiply by 2.

questions.text: You bought 2 packs of juice boxes at $3.80 each, and 3 bags of chips at $2.50 each. What is your total so far?
questions.hint: Calculate each item separately first: (2 × $3.80) and (3 × $2.50). Then add them together.

questions.text: Your current total is $15.10. You want to add a fruit platter for $12.75. Your budget is $40. How much money will you have left after buying the fruit platter?
questions.hint: Subtract both amounts from $40. First find your new total: $15.10 + $12.75, then subtract from $40.

questions.text: For dessert you have two choices: a box of 24 chocolate chip cookies for $6.00, or individual cookies at $0.35 each. You need 20 cookies. Which is cheaper, and by how much?
questions.hint: Calculate the cost of 20 individual cookies (20 × $0.35) and compare to the box price of $6.00.
questions.explanation: 20 individual cookies: 20 × $0.35 = $7.00. One box of 24: $6.00 (with 4 extra cookies!). Box saves: $7.00 − $6.00 = $1.00.

decision.prompt: You bought juice boxes, chips, a fruit platter, and a cookie box. Your total is $33.85, and you have $6.15 left. What do you do with the remaining budget?

options.text: Save it for the next class event
options.outcome: Great financial thinking! Setting aside leftover funds shows discipline and helps your class plan ahead for future events.

options.text: Buy extra treats to surprise the class
options.outcome: You made everyone happy! Sometimes spending to create joy for others is a great use of extra funds — especially when you stayed under budget.
Responsible and honest! Returning unused funds shows integrity and gives your teacher flexibility for other class needs.

reflection.prompt: What was the hardest part of staying under your $40 budget? If you had to do this shopping trip again, what would you do differently?

badge.name: Budget Boss
badge.description: Planned a class party snack table under $40
